failures.title: Jeep 55263087 1.3 MultiAir Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: MultiAir III actuator failure - irregular engine operation
items.whatHappens: The MultiAir III system uses hydraulic actuators to control valve lift and timing. Partial blockage of the actuators can cause irregular engine operation, loss of power, difficult starting, and temporary three-cylinder operation. These problems are often linked to failure to replace the oil within prescribed intervals or the use of non-compliant oil.
items.repairVsReplace: MultiAir actuator replacement is a specialist job (£800-£1,500 at an independent). In severe cases, the entire cylinder head may need replacement. Regular oil changes with the correct 5W-30 specification are essential for prevention.

items.title: Timing chain wear - premature replacement
items.whatHappens: The GSE-T4 engine uses a timing chain with a relatively short service life. Chain wear can cause rattling on cold start, timing-related fault codes, and if ignored, catastrophic engine damage.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain replacement is a significant job (£800-£1,500 at an independent). If the chain has jumped timing, cylinder head or piston damage may have occurred - at which point a full engine replacement becomes necessary.

items.title: Oil leaks - rear main crankshaft oil seal
items.whatHappens: Some 1.3L MultiAir engines have experienced oil leaks from the rear main crankshaft oil seal. This can cause oil drips and, if ignored, low oil pressure.
items.repairVsReplace: Rear main seal replacement is a labour-intensive job (£400-£800) as the transmission must be removed. If oil pressure has dropped due to the leak, bearing damage may have occurred.

items.title: Engine mount issues - abnormal noise
items.whatHappens: Some vehicles have experienced issues with the right-hand side engine mount, causing abnormal noise.
items.repairVsReplace: Engine mount replacement is a straightforward job (£200-£400 at an independent).

failures.goodYearsLine: The GSE-T4 1.3 MultiAir was introduced in 2018 and produced until around 2022. Later builds (2020+) have received ongoing refinements, though the MultiAir system remains complex and requires meticulous maintenance. Regular oil changes using the correct 5W-30 specification are essential for longevity.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 55263087 1.3 MultiAir
variants.intro: The 55263087 code is part of Stellantis's GSE engine family. However, there is significant confusion around this code - it is used for both petrol and diesel variants in different applications. Where to find the engine code: - On the engine block - a stamped label on the front or side of the engine - On the V5C registration document under "Engine number" - On the driver's door pillar or under-bonnet VIN/engine sticker - Via a VIN decoder - enter your full 17-digit VIN online to confirm the factory engine code Common confusions: | Similar code | Difference | Link | |--------------|------------|------| | 55263087 (2.0 Diesel) | 2.0-litre MultiJet diesel used in Renegade and Compass - completely different engine | [55263087 2.0 diesel] | | 55282328 (EYF) | 1.3T 180 hp petrol (bioethanol/gasoline) variant - different calibration | [55282328 engine] | | 55263624 | 1.4 MultiAir Turbo - predecessor engine | [55263624 engine] | | EBT | Sales code for 2.0 diesel variant | - | | EYF / EYH / EYJ | Sales codes for 1.3 petrol variants | - |

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 55263087 1.3 MultiAir - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 55263087 1.3 MultiAir can be a viable option for older Renegade or Compass examples. However - insist on documented service history with evidence of regular oil changes using the correct 5W-30 specification. The MultiAir system is highly sensitive to oil quality and condition. Timing chain history is also critical; walk away from any unit with rattling on cold start. Given the relative newness of this engine (2018-2022), many used units will be lower-mileage, but check for MultiAir actuator and timing chain issues regardless.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper 55263087 recon addresses the known weak points - MultiAir III actuator inspection and replacement where necessary, timing chain replacement (with updated components), full gasket and seal renewal, and oil system flush. The turbocharger is also inspected and serviced. With 12-24 months warranty, this is the safest route for most owners. Given the complexity of the MultiAir III system, specialist knowledge is essential.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild of the 55263087 is usually only justified for low-mileage, high-value examples (e.g., a cherished Renegade Trailhawk with under 50,000 miles). The rebuild must include new MultiAir actuators, new timing chain and tensioner, new turbocharger (or full rebuild), and new pistons and rings. This is the "zero-risk" option - but at £3,500-£5,000 supply-only, it's only viable for vehicles worth over £10,000.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting through our network of vetted UK Jeep and Stellantis specialists - supply-only or full supply and fit, with nationwide delivery and warranty cover on every reconditioned and rebuilt unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 55263087 sits in vehicles with modest to mid-range values - a 2018 Renegade may be worth £6,000-£12,000, while a 2022 Compass might be worth £10,000-£18,000. For most applications, the vehicle value comfortably exceeds replacement cost. For lower-value examples (sub-£7,000), a used engine with documented service history may be the most financially sensible route. For higher-value or off-road-use vehicles, a reconditioned unit with MultiAir and timing chain addressed is the better long-term investment. Always evaluate the specific vehicle's condition and value before committing to a replacement.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Jeep 55263087 1.3 MultiAir engine?
items.answer: The most common failures are MultiAir III actuator failure (causing irregular engine operation and loss of power) and timing chain wear (rattling on cold start). MultiAir actuator failure typical onset is 40,000-80,000 miles; often linked to poor oil maintenance. Timing chain wear typical onset is 50,000-90,000 miles; can cause catastrophic damage if ignored. Oil leaks from the rear main seal are also reported.

items.answer: A used 55263087 is viable only if it has full documented service history with regular oil changes using the correct 5W-30 specification - the MultiAir system is highly sensitive to oil quality. Given the relative newness (2018-2022), many used units will be lower-mileage, but check for MultiAir actuator issues regardless. A reconditioned unit is the better choice for most owners, as it addresses the MultiAir actuator, timing chain, and includes a 12-24 month warranty. items.question: Why is there confusion around the 55263087 engine code?
items.answer: The 55263087 code is used for both the 1.3-litre petrol MultiAir and the 2.0-litre diesel MultiJet in some databases - they are completely different engines. 55263087 (1.3L petrol) is the GSE-T4 MultiAir III producing 130-180 hp. 55263087 (2.0L diesel) is the MultiJet diesel with different displacement, fuel system, and ancillaries. Always confirm displacement (1.3L vs 2.0L) and fuel type (petrol vs diesel) before ordering - fitting the wrong engine is a costly mistake.
bullets: 55263087 (2.0L diesel): MultiJet diesel, different displacement, fuel system, and ancillaries

items.question: How do I confirm my Jeep has the 55263087 1.3 MultiAir engine code?
items.answer: Check three places: the engine block itself (a stamped label on the front or side of the inline-four), your V5C registration document under 'Engine number', and use a VIN decoder online with your full 17-digit VIN to pull the factory build sheet. Given the confusion with the 2.0L diesel sharing the same code, always verify displacement (1.3L) and fuel type before ordering.
